correctness_confidence.basis: Every theorem statement, algebraic proof step (Equations 1-18), Krein and absolute-bound inequality, exhaustive n <= 1200 Diophantine enumeration, 16-graph Table 1 rational entry, and plotted numerical value in Figures 1-3 was independently checked and verified exact with zero mathematical or arithmetic errors.

novelty.basis: Establishes an exact conference-extremal lower bound on Cesaro return probability, the complement sign-flip and Seidel midpoint law for off-diagonal imbalance, a new infinite polynomial parameter family solving the non-conference off-diagonal uniformity Diophantine system anchored by the ternary Golay dual coset graph, and an unconditional polytope separation between off-diagonal Cesaro uniformity and generalized UAM.

reproducibility.basis: All derivations are self-contained and written in exact rational/polynomial form, Table 1 gives exact reduced fractions for all 16 canonical SRGs, and Section 5 transparently delineates what is verified by constructive Lean 4.36.0 theorems versus exact rational Python certificates and paper proofs.

rigor.basis: Proofs are complete and precise, carefully handling irrational conference eigenvalues via Galois conjugation, explicitly distinguishing parameter-family feasibility from graph realization for t >= 3, and cleanly separating necessary [-1, 1]^3 polytope intersection from sufficient trigonometric moment realizability.

significance.basis: Provides a crisp structural classification of Cesaro and generalized uniform average mixing on primitive strongly regular graphs, resolving whether non-conference off-diagonal Cesaro uniformity yields UAM (negatively, unconditionally for the entire t-family) while unifying 16-vertex Hadamard-involution IUM results.

summary: This manuscript establishes three exact structural theorems for continuous-time quantum walks U(t) = e^{-itA} on primitive strongly regular graphs SRG(n, k, lambda, mu). Theorem 1 proves strict rationality of the Cesaro average mixing matrix \widehat{M} (even for irrational conference graphs via Galois conjugation), an unconditional return-probability barrier \widehat{M}_{uu} >= (n^2 - 2n + 3)/(2n^2) > 1/n attained iff G is a conference graph, and the closed-form off-diagonal imbalance law \widehat{M}_{adj} - \widehat{M}_{nonadj} = 2(n - 2k + lambda - mu)/(n\Delta), which flips sign under complementation and vanishes iff the regular Seidel eigenvalue bisects the two nontrivial Seidel eigenvalues. Theorem 2 reduces non-conference off-diagonal Cesaro uniformity to a Diophantine divisibility condition, constructs an infinite polynomial parameter family n(t) = (t + 1)(4t + 1)^2 passing both Krein inequalities for all t >= 1 and the absolute bound iff t >= 2 (realized at t = 2 by the ternary Golay dual coset graph SRG(243, 110, 37, 60)), and rules out all non-family survivors up to n <= 1200. Theorem 3 uses affine cosine moment lines c_1(c_3), c_2(c_3) to prove that every member t >= 1 of the off-diagonal Cesaro-uniform family violates |c_1| <= 1 (max c_1 <= -12 < -1), separating off-diagonal Cesaro uniformity from generalized UAM, while providing empty-polytope UAM no-go results for Schlafli and Higman-Sims, exact 16 x 16 Hadamard-involution IUM at t = pi/4 on Clebsch, L_2(4), and Shrikhande, and a 16-graph exact rational mixing atlas.
strengths: Exact, completely verified closed-form algebraic proofs across all three theorems, including clean treatment of irrational conference spectra via Galois conjugation over Q(sqrt(n)).

Discovery of the infinite polynomial parameter family (10) solving the non-conference off-diagonal uniformity Diophantine system, with exact Krein K_1/K_2 verification and sharp t = 1 vs. t >= 2 absolute-bound dichotomy anchored by the ternary Golay graph.
Sharp conceptual separation between off-diagonal Cesaro uniformity and generalized UAM via Theorem 3(a), proving max c_1(c_3) = -(16t^3 + 8t^2 + t - 1)/2 <= -12 < -1 unconditionally for all t >= 1.
Exact 16-graph rational mixing atlas (Table 1) and explicit 16 x 16 Hadamard-involution IUM analysis at t = pi/4 distinguishing L_2(4) from Shrikhande.

Honest and transparent verification-scope boundaries in Section 5 separating machine-checked algebraic identities from exact rational matrix/enumeration certificates and pen-and-paper spectral derivations.
weaknesses: For t >= 3 in the infinite parameter family (10) (such as the t = 3 survivor n = 676), graph existence is open; the paper properly presents (10) as a parameter family rather than a proven infinite family of realized graphs, though the prose phrase 'isolates a single infinite polynomial family' on page 4 is slightly stronger than what is proved beyond n <= 1200 (especially given the non-family Diophantine root at n = 289).

For graphs with nonempty [-1, 1]^3 moment-line intersections (e.g., Petersen, GQ(2,2), conference graphs with n >= 9), Remark 1 correctly notes that trigonometric moment realizability on R_{>= 0} remains an additional requirement not resolved in full generality here.

Formal Lean 4 verification covers the algebraic, Diophantine, and moment-line identities, whereas the Bose-Mesner spectral decomposition, Galois-conjugation argument, and n <= 1200 / 16-graph computations rest on Sections 2-4 and the external exact-rational Python artifact.
strong_novelty_candidates: Universal Cesaro return-probability barrier (n^2 - 2n + 3)/(2n^2) > 1/n with iff conference-graph extremality and exact off-diagonal complement sign-flip / Seidel midpoint law (Theorem 1).
Infinite non-conference off-diagonal Cesaro-uniform polynomial family n(t) = (t + 1)(4t + 1)^2 with t = 1 vs. t >= 2 absolute-bound dichotomy and exhaustive n <= 1200 classification (Theorem 2).
Unconditional empty-polytope UAM no-go theorem for the entire off-diagonal Cesaro-uniform t-family, proving that constant off-diagonal Cesaro mixing does not imply generalized UAM (Theorem 3(a)).
